{
  "name": "dev-hooks",
  "description": "Polyglot dev-workflow hooks for Claude Code: auto-lint on edit, verify tests/linters before stopping, a PreToolUse dangerous-command guard (catastrophic commands, plus an ask before a secret value would be printed into the transcript — cat .env, bws secret get, echo $TOKEN), per-prompt JSONL logging (plus opt-in per-hook fire telemetry via DEV_HOOKS_FIRE_LOG) that feeds the weekly automation review's add/retire passes, a per-prompt intent-check that nudges Claude to restate the goal and non-goals when a task prompt says what to do but not why or what's out of scope, and reminder hooks for plaintext secrets, leftover debug statements, missing tests, multi-session plans, review-before-finishing, verbose comments added this session, end-of-session memory capture, dev-env-standard gaps, Dockerfile layer ordering (hadolint on write), popover/tooltip positioning, database-migration safety (reversibility/backfill/lock-aware DDL), web accessibility gaps (alt/labels/keyboard), string-interpolated SQL injection, swallowed exceptions, GitHub Actions supply-chain security (SHA-pinning + ref resolution), watching the CI run after a git push, inline-SVG-to-icon-library, use-the-framework-generator scaffolding, outdated dependency pins, large uncommitted changes, a plain-language per-file change summary before finishing, and a self-stocking/self-advertising personal CLI-script library (SessionStart index of your saved tools + end-of-session nudge to keep reusable one-offs). Also ships a Claude Code mod (2.1.287+): /context-bar toggles a stacked context-window bar above the prompt, one color per /context category, and session facts records what each session did as it happens (skills incl. inside subagents, subagent dispatches, per-repo edits with net growth, the command hooks' Stop verdict), shown by /session-facts; on Stop it runs the dev-hooks Stop hooks itself and hands Claude their reasons as one block (the command hooks stand down for that session, and run as before where mods are off), passing them the session facts so a review or other skill run inside a subagent counts. After a git push it also watches that push's GitHub Actions runs itself (selected by head sha via gh): progress in the status line, a toast when they end, a pass noted in the conversation and a failure submitted as a prompt that wakes Claude, while ci-watch-reminder stands down. It also records whether Claude acted on each Stop nudge (a remedy per hook, resolved at the next Stop: review skill or review agent, compress-comments skill, memory write, test written, verify-work passing), shown by /session-facts nudges as an acted-on rate per hook and exported to ~/.claude/automation-review/stop-nudges.json for the weekly automation review. When the dangerous-command guard asks, the mod puts the question to the person in Claude Code's own dialog, which auto mode can't answer for them (unanswered: refuses after 2 minutes, or the DEV_HOOKS_GUARD_DIALOG_TIMEOUT set in settings or in front of the command). Ships the companion skills the hooks point at: dev-env-setup (mise + hk + CI + gitleaks + zizmor & actionlint GitHub Actions checks + a version-sync gate asserting every file that pins a toolchain or service version names the same one and every CI setup step reads that pin + project-docs standard, version-tracked, with a fleet mode that discovers every stamped repo via fleet_roster.sh and backfills them after a bump), github-actions (workflow supply-chain security checklist + actionlint & zizmor static analysis + fleet-wide SHA-pin/bump), dependency-upgrade (bump JS/Ruby/Python/Actions deps to latest with changelog-aware major handling and test-gated incremental commits), env-to-fnox (migrate plaintext .env secrets to fnox, with an optional migrate_env_to_fnox.py automation for the Bitwarden Secrets Manager default), dockerfile (cache-friendly layer ordering + gotchas), popovers-tooltips (collision-aware positioning with Floating UI in a Stimulus controller, plus Tippy/Flowbite/native Popover API), accessibility (on-demand WCAG 2.2/ARIA audit of changed frontend files with a heuristic a11y_audit.py, plus Rails/Hotwire + React fixes), tailwind (design tokens, taming class soup via component extraction, dark mode, responsive, and accessibility), design-process (a Discover → Define → Deliver design process for agents, adapted near-verbatim from Anshu Chimala's 'How to turn your AI into a world-class designer': seed variety from outside the model with a random string or a wild named inspiration, write a design brief and review it against the generic default before code, iterate with a fresh-context screenshot-only design-critic subagent bounded to two rounds with hard exits, settle the imagery route (key, MCP, real assets, or the user's explicit type-only call) at the gate and fill every visual slot with generated or real imagery by default, then polish by subtraction and finish with a voice pass over all copy via the writing plugin's voice-profile skill — plus a consolidated anti-slop reference distilled from the best-rated public design skills, severity-ranked by who notices), data-before-design (before any view of stored data: name the decision the view serves so every field earns its place and prominence tracks decision weight rather than query convenience, profile every field the view will show and state the numbers — including p95 length, not just the mean, and what any displayed number can be compared against — then mock several layouts from real records and let the person choose, covering all six states (ideal, empty, partial, loading, error, done) and the stress case that volume extremes never surface, and on a page with several cards fix one category table (colour, name, order) so no colour means two things across cards; paired with a UserPromptSubmit hook that fires on build-a-view prompts), worktree-setup (provision a freshly-created git worktree: trust its mise.toml, copy gitignored secrets/config like Rails master.key and .env from the main checkout, and re-mark shebang scripts executable, plus opt-in per-worktree port+database isolation via a committed .worktree-isolate.conf so parallel worktrees don't collide), compress-comments (review the comments a session's work added and cut them down, delete-biased around one survival rule — a comment survives only if it states something the code cannot show — with docstrings compressed but never deleted and lint directives untouched, plus a measured density budget and register rule: human codebases converge on ~10 comment lines per 100 code lines written as 7-8 word fragments, so past ~15% the skill ranks instead of filtering and rewrites survivors as fragments), deslop (de-LLMify the current diff in a fresh-context subagent whose brief the skill carries verbatim, because the agent that wrote the code knows why every comment is there and so finds every comment necessary: a Tier A delete-silently / Tier B fix-and-report / Tier C propose-only catalogue covering verbosity, defensive scaffolding, never-firing fallbacks, type escapes and second-way duplication, with a dependency-free slop_scan.py pairing high-precision line rules against the file-level metrics no line rule can carry — comment density, comment register, god-file size — tuned against four pre-2023 codebases for a tenfold separation between human and AI-written code), and repo-review (whole-repository severity-ranked audit across correctness, performance, smells, architecture, security, test health, dev-env, dependencies, CI supply-chain, secrets, and — for web repos — accessibility and docs; delegates to the specialist skills/commands and ships a read-only detect_stack.sh preflight; report-only, stack-agnostic counterpart to rails-audit), and script-library (genericize a one-off script into a standalone PEP 723 / uv-run CLI with a # short-description: line and save it to a library root — ~/.local/bin or a cloned, shareable scripts repo with subdirectories, configured via a PATH-style colon-separated DEV_HOOKS_SCRIPT_DIR — where the recursive script-index hook surfaces it next session), api-scraping (reverse-engineer the private JSON/GraphQL API behind a site instead of scraping HTML: gate on robots.txt/ToS, capture a HAR, find the data-carrying request with the bundled har_scan.py, minimize the request to only the headers/auth it needs, generate a paginating/rate-limited/resumable client, and escalate only as far as needed — headers → cookies/token → curl_cffi TLS impersonation → headless browser — with a sideways rung 5 that hands the user a paced, fail-closed fetch loop for their own devtools console, and a hard stop at bot challenges including Cloudflare's silent managed challenge, naming the rationalizations that dress a bypass up as an escalation), off-topic-improvements (drain a repo's plans/off-topic-improvements.md backlog: triage each parked item do-now/defer/drop, land each addressed item as its own atomic commit, and remove it from the file as it lands so the backlog stays a short live list), the standalone loop-oversight (before running an iterating loop — a /loop, a /schedule routine, or a Workflow fan-out — set up the three things that keep it reviewable: a canonical ledger, an explicit bound (max iterations / token budget / until-N-empty), and an independent verify pass that isn't the writing agent; picks the substrate by how closely you can watch and keeps unattended loops to PR-per-unit with no auto-merge), agent-brief (write a task brief for an agent aimed at an outcome not a method: a fill-in-order GOAL/WHY/DONE-WHEN/DON'T/AUTONOMY/PROVE-IT skeleton with a near-empty method box, the companion teacher to the intent-check hook), and expose-service (make a service on an internal or private host reachable and keep it reachable: pick the narrowest exposure for the audience — ssh -L/SOCKS, Tailscale Serve, Tailscale VIP Services for per-service hostnames, Cloudflare Tunnel + Access, public reverse proxy — then arm a detached systemd-run recovery before any change that can cut your own access, walk an outward reachability ladder (process → bind address → proxy-to-origin → DNS → TLS) instead of guessing, make it survive a reboot with a watchdog that catches a hung daemon and won't undo a human, and audit for a second unintended way in; references cover Tailscale serve/VIP-Services traps, the public edge where Access gates only at the edge and Authenticated Origin Pulls need orange-clouded hosts, and reachability triage).",
